definition_zh: 比率；速率；价格；费率；评价；认为
definition_en: a measure of how often or how fast something happens; a fixed charge or price; to judge the value or quality of something; to consider someone or something in a particular way
core_image: 仪表盘上按固定间隔跳动的指针
scene: 实验室的仪器每隔一会儿跳动一次，屏幕上留下一串均匀的数字。The heart rate rose as the runner climbed the hill.
sceneCN: 这里 rate 是「速率」（第 1 个义项：某事物发生的频繁程度或快慢）；句意为跑步者爬坡时心率上升。画面里可留意：规律跳动的仪器、屏幕上均匀的数字。

derivatives.zh: rate 加 -ed，指被评为某种等级的
与 rate 同源的拉丁词，指两个数量之比
over- 与 rate 复合，指高估

senses.title: A measure of frequency or speed
senses.definition: a measure of how often or how fast something happens, often per unit of time
senses.definitionCN: 衡量某事发生频率或快慢的量，常以单位时间为准
senses.example: The heart rate rose as the runner climbed the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 跑步者爬坡时心率上升。
senses.why: Rate began as a settled, calculated amount, and measuring how often something happens is exactly such a calculation.
senses.whyCN: rate 最初指算定的数量，而衡量某事发生多频繁，正属这类计算。

senses.title: A fixed price or charge
senses.definition: a fixed amount charged for a service, a room or a unit of goods
senses.definitionCN: 为服务、房间或单位商品收取的固定金额
senses.example: The hotel charges a nightly rate of two hundred pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店每晚收费两百英镑。
senses.why: A rate is a sum fixed by agreement or rule, so the word naturally named the price set for a service.
senses.whyCN: rate 是按约定或规则定下的数额，这个词便自然用来指为服务定出的价格。

senses.title: To judge value
senses.definition: to judge the value, quality or performance of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 评判某人或某物的价值、质量或表现
senses.example: Critics rated the film highly.
senses.exampleCN: 影评人给这部影片很高评价。
senses.why: Once a rate was a fixed measure, the verb could mean to place something at a particular point on that measure.
senses.whyCN: rate 既是一种固定的衡量，动词便可指把某物放到这一尺度上的特定位置。

senses.title: To consider as
senses.definition: to regard someone or something as having a particular quality or standing
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物看作具有某种品质或地位
senses.example: He is rated as one of the best players.
senses.exampleCN: 他被认为是最好的球员之一。
senses.why: Judging a thing easily becomes placing it in a class, so to rate came to mean to regard something as being of a certain kind.
senses.whyCN: 评判一物很容易变成把它归入某一类，于是 to rate 逐渐意为「把某物看作某类」。

intro.en: Rate comes from Latin rata, fixed or settled by reckoning, from reri, to reckon; Old French passed it to English as a fixed share or charge.
intro.cn: rate 来自拉丁语 rata（经计算而确定的），源自动词 reri（计算、思考）；古法语把它作为固定的份额或费用传给英语。

items.en: Rata meant fixed or settled, of a sum that had been worked out and agreed.
items.cn: rata 意为确定、算定，指经过计算并获同意的一笔数额。

items.en: The root reri meant to reckon or think, so rata was what had been calculated.
items.cn: 词根 reri 意为计算或思考，因此 rata 就是被算出来的东西。

items.en: Old French rate carried the idea of a fixed share or a charge to be paid.
items.cn: 古法语 rate 带着「固定份额」或「应缴费用」的意思。

items.en: Middle English rate used the word for a fixed charge and for a measured proportion.
items.cn: 中古英语 rate 既指固定费用，也指被计量出的比例。

items.en: Modern English keeps rate for a measured proportion and a price, and adds the verb to rate, meaning to judge.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 rate 表示测得的比例与价格，并加上动词 rate，意为评判。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived forms and one confusing neighbour; the near-meaning group gathers words for speed, proportion and charge.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式与一个易混词；近义组收表示速度、比例与收费的词。

entries.definition: Judged to have a certain quality.
A small rodent, a different word.
The rate at which something moves.
The speed at which something happens.

The price asked for a service.

normalIntro.en: The word begins as a reckoned, fixed amount, then splits into a measured proportion, a set price and the act of judging.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「算定的数额」开始，随后分成测得的比例、定好的价格与评判的行为。

normal.en: Rate and ratio share a Latin root meaning to reckon.
normal.cn: rate 与 ratio 共有表示「计算」的拉丁词根。

normal.en: A heart rate counts beats per minute, a rate per unit of time.
normal.cn: heart rate 数的是每分钟的跳动，即每单位时间的速率。

normal.en: A hotel rate is a fixed price for a room.
normal.cn: hotel rate 是一间房的固定价格。

normal.en: To rate a film is to give it a score.
normal.cn: to rate a film 就是给它打分。

normal.en: Rat and rate look alike but a rat is an animal and a rate is a measure.
normal.cn: rat 与 rate 形近，但 rat 是动物，rate 是度量。

abstract.en: A rate turns the flow of time into a number you can compare.
abstract.cn: rate 把时间的流动变成一个可以比较的数字。

abstract.en: To rate something is to turn a judgment into a place on a scale.
abstract.cn: 给某物 rate，就是把一次判断变成尺度上的一个位置。

abstract.en: Every rate hides a choice of what to count and over how long.
abstract.cn: 每一个 rate 背后都藏着「数什么、数多久」的选择。

examples.en: The heart rate rose as the runner climbed the hill.
examples.cn: 跑步者爬坡时心率上升。

examples.en: The hotel charges a nightly rate of two hundred pounds.
examples.cn: 这家酒店每晚收费两百英镑。

examples.en: Critics rated the film highly.
examples.cn: 影评人给这部影片很高评价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞特」——仪表上均匀跳动的数字，记住 rate 是速率、价格，也指评价。

root: 拉丁语 rata（经计算确定的）→ 古法语 rate → 现代英语 rate；同根有 ratio、rating。拉丁语 reri 意为计算、思考。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a reckoned, fixed amount; the senses divide into a measured proportion, a set price, judging, and regarding as.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「经计算而确定的数额」；义项分为测得的比例、定好的价格、评判，以及把……看作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a meter ticking at fixed intervals, its numbers even and regular.
core.cn: 核心意象：按固定间隔跳动的仪表，数字均匀而规律。

branches.cn: 按固定间隔跳动的仪表

branches.cn: 酒店柜台上的价目牌

branches.en: critics giving a film a score

branches.en: a label pinned on a person
branches.cn: 贴在一个人身上的标签

branches.en: a measured amount and a measured price
branches.cn: 被计量的数量与被计定的价格

intro.en: The word is a Latin borrowing, and its family is built with English suffixes, a prefix and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词借自拉丁语，其词族由英语后缀、一个前缀与复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin rata, fixed by reckoning, and the verb reri, to reckon, are the recorded sources of the root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rata（经计算而确定）与动词 reri（计算）是这个词根有记录可考的来源。

definition_zh: 比率；比值；比例关系
definition_en: the relation between two amounts, showing how many times one contains the other; a proportion between parts
core_image: 天平两端各堆砝码，数目清晰可数的对比
scene: 天平两端各放着一堆砝码，数目一眼就能数清。The ratio of students to teachers is ten to one.
sceneCN: 这里 ratio 是「比率」（第 1 个义项：两个数量之间的倍数关系）；句意为学生与教师的比例是十比一。画面里可留意：天平两端的砝码、清楚的数目对比。

collocations.phrase: the ratio of A to B
collocations.zh: A 与 B 的比率

derivatives.zh: 与 ratio 同源的拉丁词，指定量、配给
ratio 加 -al，指理性的、合理的
ratio 加 -cin- 与 -ation，指（正式的）推理

senses.title: The relation between two amounts
senses.definition: the relation between two amounts, showing how many times one contains the other
senses.definitionCN: 两个数量之间的关系，表明一个包含另一个多少次
senses.example: The ratio of students to teachers is ten to one.
senses.exampleCN: 学生与教师的比例是十比一。
senses.why: Latin ratio meant a reckoning, and a reckoning of two amounts against each other is exactly a ratio.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ratio 意为计算，而把两个数量相互算一算，正是一个比率。

senses.title: A proportion between parts
senses.definition: a proportion in which parts are compared with one another or with the whole
senses.definitionCN: 各部分相互比较或与整体比较时的比例关系
senses.example: The recipe gives the ratio of flour to water.
senses.exampleCN: 这份食谱给出了面粉与水的比例。
senses.why: Once two amounts could be compared, the word served for any ordered comparison of parts, as in a recipe or a design.
senses.whyCN: 一旦两个数量可以相互比较，这个词便用于任何有次序的部分比较，如食谱或设计中的配比。

intro.en: Ratio is the Latin word for reckoning, calculation and reason; it comes from reri, to reckon or think, and English borrowed it directly.
intro.cn: ratio 是拉丁语中表示计算、推算与理性的词；它源自动词 reri（计算、思考），英语直接借用了它。

items.en: Ratio meant a reckoning or a calculation, and also the faculty of reason that makes counting possible.
items.cn: ratio 意为计算或推算，也指使计数成为可能的理性能力。

items.en: The verb reri meant to reckon or think, and ratio was the noun of that act.
items.cn: 动词 reri 意为计算或思考，ratio 是这一动作的名词。

items.en: Roman writers used ratio for the relation between numbers, the sense that mathematics still keeps.
items.cn: 罗马作者用 ratio 指数字之间的关系，这一意思仍留在数学中。

items.en: English took ratio straight from Latin in the mathematical and general sense of a relation between amounts.
items.cn: 英语直接从拉丁语借入 ratio，用于数学及一般意义上「数量之间的关系」。

items.en: Modern English uses ratio for a quotient, for a proportion between parts, and in fixed phrases such as the golden ratio.
items.cn: 现代英语用 ratio 指比值、部分之间的比例，并见于 golden ratio 等固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin root and one near form; the near-meaning group gathers words for proportion and comparison.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词根的词与一个近形词；近义组收表示比例与比较的词。

entries.definition: A measure or a speed, related in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 一种度量或速度，意义相关。

entries.definition: A fixed share of food or supplies.
entries.definitionCN: 食物或物资的定量份额。

entries.definition: A set of reasons for something.
entries.definitionCN: 为某事给出的一套理由。

entries.definition: The relation of one part to another or to the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 一部分与另一部分或与整体的关系。

entries.definition: A part of a whole, often written as one number over another.
entries.definitionCN: 整体的一部分，常写成一个数在另一个数之上。

entries.definition: A rate or proportion expressed out of a hundred.
entries.definitionCN: 以百为基数表达的比率或比例。

entries.definition: A part given to or held by one person or group.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人或某群体的一份。

normalIntro.en: The word is Latin reckoning, and every sense is a way of putting two amounts side by side to see how they compare.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「计算」，每个义项都是把两个数量并排摆好、看它们如何相比的方式。

normal.en: Ratio and rate both come from reckoning, but ratio compares two amounts while rate measures one against time.
normal.cn: ratio 与 rate 都源于计算，但 ratio 比较两个数量，rate 则用一个量去量时间。

normal.en: The ratio of A to B is written as a pair of numbers, often with a colon.
normal.cn: A 与 B 的比率写成一对数，常用冒号隔开。

normal.en: A recipe works by ratio: so much flour for so much water.
normal.cn: 食谱靠 ratio 运作：多少面粉配多少水。

normal.en: The golden ratio is a fixed proportion that appears in art and nature.
normal.cn: 黄金比例是一个固定的比例，出现在艺术与自然之中。

normal.en: Ration is the same root, a fixed share measured out.
normal.cn: ration 同根，指称量出来的一份定量。

abstract.en: A ratio turns a comparison into a number you can carry away.
abstract.cn: ratio 把一次比较变成一个可以带走的数字。

abstract.en: To give a ratio is to say how much of one thing sits beside another.
abstract.cn: 给出一个 ratio，就是说明一物相对另一物有多少。

abstract.en: Every ratio chooses what to count and what to leave out.
abstract.cn: 每一个 ratio 都在选择数什么、略去什么。

examples.en: The ratio of students to teachers is ten to one.
examples.cn: 学生与教师的比例是十比一。

examples.en: The recipe gives the ratio of flour to water.
examples.cn: 这份食谱给出了面粉与水的比例。

examples.en: Mix the paint in a ratio of two parts blue to one part white.
examples.cn: 按两份蓝配一份白的比例调颜料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞笑」——天平两端一称，数目比出来了，记住 ratio 是比率、比例。

root: 拉丁语 ratio（计算、理性）→ 英语 ratio；源自动词 reri（计算、思考）。同根有 rate、ration、rational、rationale。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a reckoning of two amounts; the senses divide into a quotient and a proportion between parts.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是对两个数量的计算；义项分为比值与部分之间的比例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: weights piled on both pans of a balance, their numbers plainly compared.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平两端堆着砝码，数目清楚地相互比较。

definition_zh: 理性的；合理的；有理数的；心智健全的
definition_en: based on reason rather than feeling; sensible and logical; expressible as a ratio of two integers; able to think clearly
core_image: 案头一列摆得整整齐齐、编号清楚的卡片
scene: 会议桌旁，人人按次序发言，论点一条条摆得明白。She gave a rational explanation for the delay.
sceneCN: 这里 rational 是「合理的」（第 2 个义项：合乎道理与逻辑）；句意为她为延误给出了合理的解释。画面里可留意：按次序的发言、条理清楚的论点。

pos.zh: 理性的；合理的；有理数的；心智健全的

derivatives.zh: rational 加 -ly，指理性地、合理地
ir- 与 rational 复合，指非理性的

senses.title: Guided by reason
senses.definition: based on reason rather than on feeling or impulse
senses.definitionCN: 基于道理而非情感或冲动
senses.example: A rational person checks the facts before deciding.
senses.exampleCN: 理性的人会先核对事实再作决定。
senses.why: Rational comes from Latin ratio, reason itself, so the adjective first describes a mind that works by reckoning.
senses.whyCN: rational 来自拉丁语 ratio，即理性本身，因此这个形容词首先描述按计算运作的心智。

senses.title: Sensible and logical
senses.definition: sensible, logical and free of contradiction, used of explanations, plans and choices
senses.definitionCN: 合乎道理、有逻辑且不自相矛盾，用于解释、计划与选择
senses.example: She gave a rational explanation for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 她为延误给出了合理的解释。
senses.why: If a mind works by reason, then what such a mind produces is also called rational: a sound, well-grounded account.
senses.whyCN: 如果心智按理性运作，那么这种心智产出的东西也被称为 rational：一个站得住脚、有根据的说法。

senses.title: Expressible as a ratio
senses.definition: of a number, able to be written as the ratio of two whole numbers
senses.definitionCN: 指一个数可以写成两个整数之比
senses.example: One half is a rational number.
senses.exampleCN: 二分之一是一个有理数。
senses.why: Mathematics took the word literally: a rational number is one that can be expressed as a ratio.
senses.whyCN: 数学把这个词按字面使用：有理数就是可以表示成比率的数。

senses.title: Able to think clearly
senses.definition: able to think and judge clearly, not confused or insane
senses.definitionCN: 能够清楚思考和判断，未混乱或失常
senses.example: The patient remained rational throughout the night.
senses.exampleCN: 这位病人整夜都保持清醒理智。
senses.why: Reason is the mark of a sound mind, so rational came to describe a person whose thinking is intact.
senses.whyCN: 理性是健全心智的标志，因此 rational 也用来形容思维完好的人。

intro.en: Rational comes from Latin rationalis, belonging to ratio, reason or reckoning; English borrowed it to describe what follows reason.
intro.cn: rational 来自拉丁语 rationalis，意为属于 ratio（理性、计算）的；英语借它来描述合乎理性的事物。

items.en: Ratio meant reckoning and reason, the power by which amounts and arguments are worked out.
items.cn: ratio 意为计算与理性，是推算数量与论证的力量。

items.en: Rationalis meant belonging to reason, and it described a thinking being and a well-grounded argument alike.
items.cn: rationalis 意为属于理性的，既形容会思考的存在，也形容有根据的论证。

items.en: English took rationalis as rational, keeping the link between reason and sound judgment.
items.cn: 英语把 rationalis 借作 rational，保留理性与健全判断之间的联系。

items.en: Mathematicians used rational for numbers that can be written as a ratio of integers.
items.cn: 数学家把 rational 用于可写成整数之比的数。

items.en: Modern English uses rational for reasoned thought, sensible plans, such numbers, and a sound mind.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rational 指有理性的思维、合理的计划、这类数，以及健全的心智。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the root word and its close forms; the near-meaning group gathers words for what is reasonable and sane.
note.cn: 形近组收词根词与近形词；近义组收表示合理与清醒的词。

entries.definition: A set of reasons for something.
entries.definitionCN: 为某事给出的一套理由。

entries.definition: Fair and based on good sense.

normalIntro.en: The word begins as belonging to reason, then passes to sound arguments, to numbers written as ratios, and to a mind that is intact.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「属于理性」开始，转到有根据的论证，再到可写成比率的数，最后到完好的心智。

normal.en: Rational comes from ratio, reason, so a rational act is one that reason can account for.
normal.cn: rational 来自 ratio（理性），因此理性的行为是理性能够解释的行为。

normal.en: A rational explanation is one that holds together without contradiction.
normal.cn: 合理的解释是前后一致、不自相矛盾的解释。

normal.en: A rational number is simply a number that can be written as a ratio.
normal.cn: 有理数就是可以写成一个比的数。

normal.en: Rational and rationale are close, but rationale is the set of reasons behind a choice.
normal.cn: rational 与 rationale 相近，但 rationale 是一项选择背后的那套理由。

normal.en: Irrational is the direct opposite, built with the negative prefix ir-.
normal.cn: irrational 是直接的反义词，由否定前缀 ir- 构成。

abstract.en: To be rational is to let reasons, not moods, decide.
abstract.cn: 理性，就是让理由而非情绪作决定。

abstract.en: A rational plan can be explained to anyone who asks why.
abstract.cn: 合理的计划能向任何追问原因的人解释清楚。

abstract.en: What is rational is not always what is kind.
abstract.cn: 合乎理性的，并不总是仁慈的。

examples.en: A rational person checks the facts before deciding.
examples.cn: 理性的人会先核对事实再作决定。

examples.en: She gave a rational explanation for the delay.
examples.cn: 她为延误给出了合理的解释。

examples.en: One half is a rational number.
examples.cn: 二分之一是一个有理数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「拉申诺」——凡事列出理由、算清条理，记住 rational 是理性的、合理的。

root: 拉丁语 ratio（计算、理性）→ rationalis（属于理性的）→ 英语 rational；同族有 rationally、rationality、rationale、irrational。

sensesIntro.en: The core is reason; the senses divide into a reasoned mind, a sound argument, a number written as a ratio, and a mind that is intact.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「理性」；义项分为有理性的心智、有根据的论证、可写成比率的数，以及健全的心智。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of cards laid out in clear numbered order, each argument in its place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排按清晰编号摆开的卡片，每条论证都各在其位。

branches.en: a person checking facts before speaking
branches.cn: 开口前先核对事实的人

branches.en: an argument that holds together
branches.cn: 前后一致、站得住脚的论证

branches.en: one half written as a ratio
branches.cn: 写成一个比的二分之一

branches.en: a patient thinking clearly through the night
branches.cn: 整夜思维清醒的病人

branches.en: a reason-driven mind and the sound argument it produces
branches.cn: 受理智驱动的心智与它产出的可靠论证

intro.en: The word is a Latin borrowing, and its family is built with Latin and English suffixes and one negative prefix.
intro.cn: 这个词借自拉丁语，其词族由拉丁语与英语后缀，以及一个否定前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin ratio, reason, and rationalis, belonging to reason, are the recorded sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ratio（理性）与 rationalis（属于理性的）是有记录可考的来源。

items.meaning: a number writable as a ratio

definition_zh: 饿极了的；贪婪的；贪得无厌的
definition_en: extremely hungry, or eager to consume something in large amounts
core_image: 一个人盯着桌上的面包，眼睛比手先动
scene: 队伍两天没吃东西，一见到面包就扑了上去。After two days without food, the group fell on the bread like ravenous animals.
sceneCN: 这里 ravenous 指饿极了的（第 1 个义项：极度饥饿）；句意为队伍两天没吃东西，一见到面包就扑了上去。

pos.zh: 饿极了的；贪婪的；贪得无厌的

senses.title: Extremely hungry
senses.definition: so hungry that food fills the mind and the body moves before it thinks
senses.definitionCN: 饿到食物占满头脑、身体先于思考而动
senses.example: After two days without food, the group fell on the bread like ravenous animals.
senses.exampleCN: 两天没吃东西之后，队伍像饿极了的野兽一样扑向面包。
senses.why: This is the physical sense, and it keeps the violence of the Latin root inside a hungry body.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体的一层，它把拉丁词根里的那股猛劲留在饥饿的身体上。

senses.title: Greedily eager for something
senses.titleCN: 贪婪渴求的；贪得无厌的
senses.definition: eager to take in something other than food, such as news, power or resources, in amounts that cannot be satisfied
senses.definitionCN: 对食物以外的东西（消息、权力、资源）渴求到无法满足
senses.example: The reporters were ravenous for any detail of the case.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们贪求这个案子的一切细节。
senses.why: The hunger moves from stomach to another appetite, while the word keeps its taking edge.
senses.whyCN: 饥饿从胃移到了另一种欲望上，而那个伸手就拿的锋芒还在。

intro.en: Ravenous comes from Latin ravinosus, 'given to seizing', from ravere, a form linked to rapacity.
intro.cn: ravenous 来自拉丁语 ravinosus（惯于夺取的），与表示掠夺的词相关。

items.en: Rapere meant to seize and carry off.
items.cn: rapere 意为抓住带走。

items.en: Ravina named a rushing or a seizure.
items.cn: ravina 指猛冲或夺取。

items.en: The adjective described a seizing hunger.
items.cn: 这个形容词描述夺取般的饥饿。

items.en: English used ravenous for extreme hunger.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪用 ravenous 指极度饥饿。

items.en: The word now also describes greedy use of resources.
items.cn: 今天这个词也描述对资源的贪婪使用。

note.en: The look-alike group is the raven- family; the near-meaning group separates starving, famished, voracious and insatiable.
note.cn: 形近组是 raven 词族；近义组把「濒饿的」「饿坏的」「贪婪的」「无法满足的」分开。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a hand reaching before the mind has spoken.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「手在头脑开口之前先伸出去」的画面。

normal.en: Ravenous shares a root with ravenous beasts and rapacity: hunger that grabs.
normal.cn: ravenous 与掠夺同根：会抓取的饥饿。

normal.en: Picture a loaf on a table and a whole group moving at once.
normal.cn: 想象桌上一条面包，一整群人在同一刻动起来。

normal.en: Say RAV-e-nus; the middle sounds like ravine.
normal.cn: 读 RAV-e-nus，中间听起来像 ravine。

normal.en: The word can describe appetite for food, news or water use.
normal.cn: 这个词可以描述对食物、消息或水资源的胃口。

normal.en: Ask whether the hunger is a body or a system.
normal.cn: 问一句：这饥饿属于一具身体，还是一个系统？

abstract.en: Ravenous describes need that has begun to look like appetite.
abstract.cn: ravenous 描述一种已经开始像胃口的需要。

abstract.en: The word makes hunger active: it reaches, it takes, it does not wait.
abstract.cn: 这个词让饥饿变成主动的：它伸手、它拿取、它不等。

abstract.en: Every economy has a ravenous edge where demand outruns supply.
abstract.cn: 每个经济体都有一条贪婪的边，那里需求跑在供给前面。

examples.en: The long walk gave the children a ravenous appetite.
examples.cn: 长途步行让孩子们胃口大开。

examples.en: The reporters were ravenous for any detail of the case.
examples.cn: 记者们急于吞下这个案子的任何细节。

examples.en: The city's ravenous consumption of water emptied the reservoir.
examples.cn: 这座城市对水的贪婪消耗掏空了水库。

dict_mnemonic.text: raven（猛夺）+ ous（充满）→ 饿得像要抢食一样。

root: 拉丁语 rapere（夺取）→ ravinosus（惯于夺取的）

sensesIntro.en: Ravenous has two senses: a body made violent by hunger, and a hunger of the mind that no amount can satisfy.
sensesIntro.cn: ravenous 有两层：被饥饿变得凶猛的身体，以及任何数量都无法满足的头脑之饥。

core.en: A HAND REACHING FIRST
core.cn: 先伸出去的手

branches.en: The body that reaches before it thinks.
branches.cn: 先伸手、后思考的身体。

branches.en: Bread, and hands moving at once.
branches.cn: 面包，以及同时伸出的手。

branches.en: Hunger moved to news, books or resources.
branches.cn: 饥饿移向消息、书本或资源。

branches.en: Food in one sense, everything else in the other.
branches.cn: 一层是食物，另一层是食物之外的一切。

branches.en: A hunger that consumption cannot end.
branches.cn: 消耗无法终止的饥饿。

intro.en: The ravenous family is built on grabbing: ravenous, ravenously and ravenousness all keep the sense of a hunger that takes.
intro.cn: ravenous 词族建立在抓取上：ravenous、ravenously、ravenousness 都保留「会拿取的饥饿」这层意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin rapere, 'to seize', gives ravina and ravinosus; the English word kept the violence and lost the Latin noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rapere（夺取）给出 ravina 与 ravinosus；英语保留暴力感，丢掉了拉丁名词。

definition_zh: 生的；未加工的；生疏的；裸露刺痛的
definition_en: not cooked; not processed or refined; inexperienced and untrained; bare and sore, of skin or nerves
core_image: 刚出矿的粗糙石块，棱角上还粘着砂粒
scene: 采石场里，刚开采出的石块粗糙发灰，棱角上还粘着砂粒。The raw material is shipped to the factory for processing.
sceneCN: 这里 raw 是「未加工的」（第 2 个义项：尚未经过处理或提炼）；句意为原材料被运往工厂加工。画面里可留意：粗糙的石块、棱角的砂粒、运石的车。

pos.zh: 生的；未加工的；生疏的；裸露刺痛的

derivatives.zh: raw 加 -ness，指生、未加工的状态
raw 加 -ly，指生硬地、赤裸地
raw 与 hide 复合，指生皮

senses.title: Not cooked
senses.definition: of food, not cooked at all
senses.definitionCN: 指食物完全没有烹煮
senses.example: Cats can eat raw meat.
senses.exampleCN: 猫可以吃生肉。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply uncooked, and it still describes food taken straight from the fireless kitchen.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是「未煮」，至今仍用来描述未经火候的食物。

senses.title: Not processed
senses.definition: of a material, not yet treated, refined or manufactured
senses.definitionCN: 指材料尚未经过处理、提炼或制造
senses.example: The raw material is shipped to the factory.
senses.exampleCN: 原材料被运往工厂。
senses.why: From uncooked food the word extended to any material that has not yet been worked into its final form.
senses.whyCN: 从「未煮的食物」扩展到任何尚未被加工成最终形态的材料。

senses.title: Inexperienced
senses.definition: new to something and not yet trained or hardened
senses.definitionCN: 刚接触某事、尚未训练或磨练的
senses.example: The raw recruits were still learning to march.
senses.exampleCN: 新兵们还在学习列队行进。
senses.why: A person who has not been through training is like material not yet worked, so raw came to mean inexperienced.
senses.whyCN: 未经训练的人就像尚未加工的材料，于是 raw 引申为「生疏」。

senses.title: Bare and sore
senses.definition: of skin or a nerve, exposed and painful, without protection
senses.definitionCN: 指皮肤或神经外露、疼痛、缺乏保护
senses.example: The cold wind stung his raw face.
senses.exampleCN: 寒风刺着他裸露发疼的脸。
senses.why: Skin stripped of its covering is exposed like unworked material, and the painful openness gave the word its sense of soreness.
senses.whyCN: 失去覆盖的皮肤就像未经处理的材料一样暴露在外，这种疼痛的暴露给了这个词「刺痛」的意思。

intro.en: Raw is a native English word from Old English hreaw, meaning uncooked, with relatives in other Germanic languages; no Latin source is recorded.
intro.cn: raw 是英语本族词，来自古英语 hreaw（未煮的），在其他日耳曼语言中有亲属词；没有拉丁语来源记录。

items.en: Hreaw meant uncooked or unprocessed, and it described food and materials alike.
items.cn: hreaw 意为未煮或未加工的，既形容食物，也形容材料。

items.en: Related forms in other Germanic languages carry the same sense of something not yet cooked or worked.
items.cn: 其他日耳曼语言中的相关形式带有同样的「尚未煮或加工」之意。

items.en: Middle English raw kept the sense of uncooked and extended it to what was rough and unfinished.
items.cn: 中古英语 raw 保留「未煮」的意思，并扩展到粗糙、未完成之物。

items.en: Because what is unworked is also untrained or uncovered, raw came to describe new soldiers and bare skin.
items.cn: 由于未加工之物也意味着未受训练或未被覆盖，raw 便用来形容新兵与裸露的皮肤。

items.en: Modern English uses raw for uncooked food, unprocessed material, inexperienced people, and exposed flesh.
items.cn: 现代英语用 raw 指生食、未加工的材料、无经验的人，以及裸露的皮肉。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and one easily confused word; the near-meaning group gathers words for the uncooked, the unrefined and the untrained.
note.cn: 形近组收复合词与一个易混词；近义组收表示生的、未精炼的、未受训练的词。

entries.definitionCN: 用生皮制成的未处理皮革。

entries.definition: Lightly cooked, easily confused with raw.
entries.definitionCN: 半熟的，容易与 raw 混淆。

entries.definition: In a natural state, not refined.
entries.definitionCN: 处于自然状态、未经精炼的。

entries.definition: Not treated by an industrial process.
New to an activity, without practice.
entries.definitionCN: 刚接触某项活动、缺乏实践的。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as uncooked, then covers unworked material, untrained people and unprotected skin, all sharing the idea of not yet finished.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「未煮」开始，随后覆盖未加工的材料、未受训练的人与未受保护的皮肤，都共享「尚未完成」这一想法。

normal.en: Raw and rare are close in the kitchen, but raw is completely uncooked while rare is lightly cooked.
normal.cn: 在厨房里 raw 与 rare 相近，但 raw 是完全没煮，rare 是略煮。

normal.en: Raw material is what a factory turns into a finished product.
normal.cn: raw material 是工厂加工成成品之前的材料。

normal.en: Raw data has not yet been cleaned or sorted.
normal.cn: raw data 是尚未清理或整理的数据。

normal.en: A raw recruit is a soldier who has not yet been trained.
normal.cn: raw recruit 是尚未受过训练的新兵。

normal.en: Raw skin is skin stripped of its covering and left sore.
normal.cn: raw skin 是失去覆盖、裸露发疼的皮肤。

abstract.en: What is raw is full of possibility but not yet usable.
abstract.cn: raw 之物充满可能，却尚不可用。

abstract.en: To be raw is to be honest and exposed at the same time.
abstract.cn: raw 既是坦诚，也是暴露。

abstract.en: Every finished thing once lay raw and unshaped.
abstract.cn: 每一件成品都曾经是未成形的原材料。

examples.en: Cats can eat raw meat.
examples.cn: 猫可以吃生肉。

examples.en: The raw material is shipped to the factory for processing.
examples.cn: 原材料被运往工厂加工。

examples.en: The raw recruits were still learning to march.
examples.cn: 新兵们还在学习列队行进。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「刚从矿里挖出的石块」——粗糙、没加工过，记住 raw 是生的、未加工的。

root: 古英语 hreaw（未煮的）→ 中古英语 raw → 现代英语 raw；同族有 rawness、rawhide、rawboned。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is not yet finished; the senses divide into uncooked food, unprocessed material, untrained people, and unprotected skin.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「尚未完成」；义项分为未煮的食物、未加工的材料、未受训练的人，以及未受保护的皮肤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rough stone just cut from the quarry, grit still clinging to its edges.
core.cn: 核心意象：刚从采石场切下的粗糙石块，棱角上还粘着砂粒。

branches.en: meat straight from the fireless kitchen
branches.cn: 未经火候的生肉

branches.en: ore and stone at the quarry face
branches.cn: 采石场工作面上的矿石与石块

branches.en: a recruit still learning to march
branches.cn: 还在学习列队的新兵

branches.en: skin stripped bare by the wind
branches.cn: 被风剥得裸露的皮肤

branches.en: unworked material and untrained people
branches.cn: 未加工的材料与未受训练的人

intro.en: The word is native and short, and its family is built from English suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词短小且为本族词，其词族由英语后缀与复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录。

items.meaning: in a bare or harsh way

definition_zh: 到达；伸手够到；达到；与…联系；可及范围
definition_en: to arrive at a place; to stretch out a hand to touch something; to attain a level or amount; to get in touch with someone; the distance within which something can be reached
core_image: 手臂伸向高架上的一只杯子
scene: 高架上的杯子有点远，手臂伸到极限才碰到杯沿。She reached the top shelf with her fingertips.
sceneCN: 这里 reach 是「伸手够到」（第 2 个义项：把手伸出去触到某物）；句意为她用指尖够到了顶层架子。画面里可留意：伸出的手臂、高架上的杯子、碰到的指尖。

pos.zh: 到达；伸手够到；达到；与…联系

derivatives.zh: reach 加 -able，指可到达的、可联系的
out 与 reach 复合，指主动外联、延伸服务
over- 与 reach 复合，指做得过头、超越能力

senses.title: To arrive at a place
senses.definition: to arrive at a place, especially after effort or a journey
senses.definitionCN: 到达某地，尤指经过努力或一段行程之后
senses.example: We reached the village before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在天黑前到达了村子。
senses.why: The oldest sense is to stretch out to a point, and arriving is stretching your journey until it touches the destination.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「伸到一点」，而抵达就是让行程一直伸到触着目的地。

senses.title: To stretch out and touch
senses.definition: to put out a hand or arm in order to touch or take something
senses.definitionCN: 伸出手或手臂去触到或拿取某物
senses.example: She reached the top shelf with her fingertips.
senses.exampleCN: 她用指尖够到了顶层架子。
senses.why: The word first pictured a hand extended until it met an object, and this literal picture is still the core.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初描绘的是手一直伸到与物体相接，这一字面画面至今仍是核心。

senses.title: To attain a level
senses.definition: to arrive at a particular level, amount or standard after a process
senses.definitionCN: 经过一个过程达到某一水平、数量或标准
senses.example: Sales reached a record high last month.
senses.exampleCN: 上个月的销售额达到了历史新高。
senses.why: If a hand can reach a height, then a process can reach a level, so the word extended from space to measure.
senses.whyCN: 手能伸到一个高度，一个过程也能达到一个水平，于是这个词从空间扩展到度量。

senses.title: To get in touch
senses.definition: to succeed in speaking or writing to someone
senses.definitionCN: 成功地与某人通话或通信
senses.example: I tried to reach him by phone all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 我一上午都在试着打电话联系他。
senses.why: Making contact is like stretching across a distance until the other person is touched, so reach came to mean communicate with.
senses.whyCN: 建立联系就像跨越距离一直伸到触着对方，于是 reach 引申为「与……沟通」。

senses.title: The distance one can reach
senses.definition: the distance or range within which something can be reached or used
senses.definitionCN: 某物能被触及或使用所及的距离或范围
senses.example: The cookies are within the child's reach.
senses.exampleCN: 饼干在孩子够得着的范围内。
senses.why: From the act of stretching came the noun for how far that stretch goes, hence the range one can cover.
senses.whyCN: 从「伸展」的动作生出名词，表示这一伸能到多远，因此就是可覆盖的范围。

intro.en: Reach is a native English word from Old English ræcan, to stretch out or extend, with relatives in other Germanic languages; no Latin source is recorded.
intro.cn: reach 是英语本族词，来自古英语 ræcan（伸出、延伸），在其他日耳曼语言中有亲属词；没有拉丁语来源记录。

items.en: Ræcan meant to stretch out or extend toward something, often a hand toward an object.
items.cn: ræcan 意为向某物伸出或延伸，常指手伸向物体。

items.en: Related Germanic verbs carry the same picture of extending toward a point.
items.cn: 相关的日耳曼语动词带有同样的「朝一点延伸」的画面。

items.en: Middle English reach widened from the hand to the journey, so one could reach a town as well as a shelf.
items.cn: 中古英语 reach 从手扩展到行程，因此既能 reach 一个架子，也能 reach 一座城镇。

items.en: As the word moved from space to levels and to people, it took in reaching a figure and reaching a person.
items.cn: 随着这个词从空间转到水平与人，它纳入了达到某个数字与联系到某个人。

items.en: Modern English uses reach for arriving, stretching, attaining, contacting, and for the range so covered.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reach 表示抵达、伸手、达到、联系，以及由此覆盖的范围。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and fixed phrases; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of arriving, attaining and contacting.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式与固定短语；近义组收表示抵达、达到与联系的动词。

entries.definition: To extend a hand or make contact.
To stretch a hand toward something.
To go too far or attempt too much.
To reach a level or goal after effort.
entries.definitionCN: 经过努力达到某一水平或目标。

entries.definition: To extend a limb or a thing.
To get in touch with someone.

normalIntro.en: The word starts with a hand stretched out, then covers journeys, levels, people and the range so covered.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从伸出的手开始，随后涵盖行程、水平、人，以及由此覆盖的范围。

normal.en: Reach and stretch share the picture of something extended toward a point.
normal.cn: reach 与 stretch 共享「某物朝一点伸展」的画面。

normal.en: You reach a shelf with a hand and reach a city with a journey.
normal.cn: 用手 reach 一个架子，用一段行程 reach 一座城市。

normal.en: Prices reaching a record high is the same word used for a level.
normal.cn: 价格 reaching a record high，是同一个词用在水平上。

normal.en: To reach someone is to stretch across the distance until contact is made.
normal.cn: to reach 某人，就是跨越距离一直伸到建立联系。

normal.en: Within reach means close enough to touch or use.
normal.cn: within reach 意为近得足以触及或使用。

abstract.en: Reach measures the distance between effort and its object.
abstract.cn: reach 衡量的是努力与其目标之间的距离。

abstract.en: What is out of reach is not always out of mind.
abstract.cn: 够不着的东西，并不总是不在心上的。

abstract.en: To reach out is to shorten a distance that other people cannot shorten alone.
abstract.cn: reach out 就是缩短一段别人无法独自缩短的距离。

examples.en: We reached the village before dark.
examples.cn: 我们在天黑前到达了村子。

examples.en: She reached the top shelf with her fingertips.
examples.cn: 她用指尖够到了顶层架子。

examples.en: I tried to reach him by phone all morning.
examples.cn: 我一上午都在试着打电话联系他。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞奇」——手臂一直伸出去，够到架子上的杯子，记住 reach 是到达、够到。

root: 古英语 ræcan（伸出、延伸）→ 中古英语 reach → 现代英语 reach；同族有 reachable、outreach、overreach。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is stretching toward a point; the senses divide into arriving, touching, attaining, contacting, and the range so covered.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「朝一点伸展」；义项分为抵达、触到、达到、联系，以及由此覆盖的范围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arm stretched to its full length toward a cup on a high shelf.
core.cn: 核心意象：手臂伸到极限，去够高架上的一只杯子。

branches.en: a traveller arriving at a village gate
branches.cn: 走到村口的旅人

branches.en: fingertips meeting a cup on a shelf
branches.cn: 指尖触到架子上的杯子

branches.en: a graph line climbing to a record
branches.cn: 攀升至最高点的曲线

branches.en: a telephone call that finally connects
branches.cn: 终于接通的电话

branches.en: a jar placed within a child's grasp
branches.cn: 放在孩子够得着处的罐子

intro.en: The word is native and short, and its family is built with English suffixes, prefixes and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词短小且为本族词，其词族由英语后缀、前缀与复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录。

definition_zh: 反应；作出反应；起化学反应；反对
definition_en: to respond to something that happens; to undergo a chemical change; to act against something in opposition
core_image: 被按到底又猛地弹回的弹簧
scene: 手指一按，弹簧被压到底，松开后立刻弹了回来。The crowd reacted with cheers when the goal was scored.
sceneCN: 这里 react 是「作出反应」（第 1 个义项：对某事作出回应）；句意为进球时人群报以欢呼。画面里可留意：被压下的弹簧、弹回的瞬间、欢呼的人群。

pos.zh: 反应；作出反应；起化学反应；反对

derivatives.zh: react 加 -or，指反应堆、反应器
react 加 -ive，指易起反应的、反应性的
re- 与 activate 复合，指使重新活跃

senses.title: To respond
senses.definition: to respond in speech, feeling or action to something that has happened
senses.definitionCN: 在言语、情感或行动上对发生之事作出回应
senses.example: The crowd reacted with cheers when the goal was scored.
senses.exampleCN: 进球时人群报以欢呼。
senses.why: Latin reagere meant to act back, and reacting is exactly acting back upon something that acted first.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 reagere 意为「回过来行动」，而 react 正是对先行动的事物回以行动。

senses.title: To undergo chemical change
senses.definition: of substances, to combine or change as a result of a chemical process
senses.definitionCN: 指物质因化学过程而结合或发生变化
senses.example: Sodium reacts violently with water.
senses.exampleCN: 钠与水剧烈反应。
senses.why: Chemistry borrowed the same idea of acting back: two substances act on each other and are changed by it.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用了同一个「相互作用」的想法：两种物质彼此作用并因此改变。

senses.title: To oppose
senses.definition: to act against something one disapproves of or resists
senses.definitionCN: 对自己不赞成或抵抗的事物采取对抗行动
senses.example: Many residents reacted against the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 许多居民反对这项新税。
senses.why: When the action back is directed against a force or a rule, the word takes the sense of resisting or opposing.
senses.whyCN: 当回过来的行动指向某种力量或规则时，这个词便有了「抵抗、反对」的意思。

intro.en: React comes from Latin reagere, built from re-, back, and agere, to do or drive; the word literally means to act back.
intro.cn: react 来自拉丁语 reagere，由 re-（回）与 agere（做、驱动）构成；字面意思就是「回过来行动」。

items.en: Agere meant to do, drive or perform, and it is the source of act, action and agent.
items.cn: agere 意为做、驱动或执行，是 act、action、agent 的来源。

items.en: The prefix re- meant back or again, so reagere pictured a force returning upon its source.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 意为向后或再次，因此 reagere 描绘的是一股力量回向它的来源。

items.en: Reagere meant to act back or to respond to an action already under way.
items.cn: reagere 意为回过来行动，或对已经在进行的动作作出回应。

items.en: English took the word as react and applied it to people, to feelings and later to chemical substances.
items.cn: 英语把这个词借作 react，先用于人、情感，后来又用于化学物质。

items.en: Modern English uses react for responses of every kind, for chemical change, and for resistance to what is imposed.
items.cn: 现代英语用 react 指各种回应、化学变化，以及对强加之事的抵抗。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived forms; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of responding and resisting.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式；近义组收表示回应与抵抗的动词。

entries.definition: A response or a chemical change.
A device or plant where a reaction takes place.
entries.definitionCN: 发生反应的装置或设施。

entries.definition: To answer or react to something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事作出回答或反应。

normalIntro.en: The word is literally act back: something acts first, and the response acts upon it in return.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词字面上就是「回过来行动」：某物先行动，回应再反过来作用于它。

normal.en: React is re- plus act, so it means to act back on what has just happened.
normal.cn: react 是 re- 加 act，意为对刚发生的事回以行动。

normal.en: People react to news, crowds react to a goal, and chemicals react with each other.
normal.cn: 人 react to 消息，人群 react to 进球，化学品彼此 react。

normal.en: React against is the phrase for resisting something you disapprove of.
normal.cn: react against 是表示抵制不赞成之事的短语。

normal.en: Reaction is the noun, reactor the thing where a reaction happens, and reactive the tendency to react.
normal.cn: reaction 是名词，reactor 是发生反应的装置，reactive 是易反应的倾向。

normal.en: A slow reaction and a quick reaction differ in time, not in the word's meaning.
normal.cn: 反应慢与反应快，差别在时间，而不在这个词的意思。

abstract.en: To react is to prove that something outside you has reached you.
abstract.cn: react 就是证明身外之物已经触及了你。

abstract.en: What we react against often tells us what we value.
abstract.cn: 我们反对的东西，常常说明我们看重什么。

abstract.en: Every action leaves the world waiting for a reaction.
abstract.cn: 每一个行动都让世界等着一个回应。

examples.en: The crowd reacted with cheers when the goal was scored.
examples.cn: 进球时人群报以欢呼。

examples.en: Sodium reacts violently with water.
examples.cn: 钠与水剧烈反应。

examples.en: Many residents reacted against the new tax.
examples.cn: 许多居民反对这项新税。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞阿克特」——弹簧被按下又弹回，记住 react 是反应、作出反应。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）+ agere（做、驱动）→ reagere（回过来行动）→ 英语 react；同族有 reaction、reactor、reactive。

sensesIntro.en: The core is acting back; the senses divide into human response, chemical change, and opposition.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「回过来行动」；义项分为人的回应、化学变化与反对。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spring pressed down and snapping back as soon as the finger lifts.
core.cn: 核心意象：弹簧被压下，手指一松便立刻弹回。

branches.en: a crowd cheering a goal
branches.cn: 为进球欢呼的人群

branches.en: sodium hissing in water
branches.cn: 在水中嘶响的钠

branches.en: residents resisting a new tax
branches.cn: 抵制新税的居民

branches.en: a human answer and a chemical answer
branches.cn: 人的回应与化学的回应

branches.en: responding to a change and resisting it
branches.cn: 对变化作出回应，也对其抵抗

intro.en: The word is a Latin borrowing, and its family is built from re-, agere and English suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个词借自拉丁语，其词族由 re-、agere 与英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin agere, to do, and reagere, to act back, are the recorded sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 agere（做）与 reagere（回过来行动）是有记录可考的来源。

definition_zh: 现实的；逼真的；可行的
definition_en: seeing things as they actually are and acting accordingly; looking or sounding like real life; achievable in practice
core_image: 画布上的静物与桌边实物几乎分不清
scene: 画布上的静物光影细腻，几乎与桌边的实物难以分辨。Her plan for the trip was realistic and cheap.
sceneCN: 这里 realistic 是「现实的」（第 1 个义项：看清实际、不空想）；句意为她的旅行计划现实而省钱。画面里可留意：细腻的光影、几乎分不清的实物与画。

derivatives.zh: un- 与 realistic 复合，指不切实际的

senses.title: Seeing things as they are
senses.definition: judging situations by what is actually true and possible rather than by wishful thinking
senses.definitionCN: 按实际真实与可能来判断情况，而非凭一厢情愿
senses.example: Her plan for the trip was realistic and cheap.
senses.exampleCN: 她的旅行计划现实而省钱。
senses.why: Realistic adds the suffix -istic to real, so it describes a mind that keeps its eye on what actually exists.
senses.whyCN: realistic 在 real 后加后缀 -istic，因此它描述始终盯着实际存在的现实的心智。

senses.title: Looking like real life
senses.definition: represented so faithfully that it looks or sounds like real life
senses.definitionCN: 表现得太忠实，以致看起来或听起来像真实生活
senses.example: The painting is so realistic that it fools the eye.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画太逼真了，骗过了眼睛。
senses.why: Art that copies what truly exists is called realistic, because its standard is the real thing outside the frame.
senses.whyCN: 摹写真实存在之物的艺术被称为 realistic，因为它的标准是画框之外的真实之物。

senses.title: Achievable
senses.definition: of a goal or expectation, possible to reach within real limits
senses.definitionCN: 指目标或期望在真实限度内可以达到
senses.example: The team set realistic goals for the first year.
senses.exampleCN: 团队为第一年设定了可行的目标。
senses.why: A goal shaped by what is actually possible rather than by desire alone is described as realistic.
senses.whyCN: 按实际可能而非单凭愿望设定的目标，被称为 realistic。

intro.en: Realistic is English real with the suffix -istic, a learned ending that came through Latin from Greek; it describes what follows the real.
intro.cn: realistic 是英语 real 加上后缀 -istic，这个词尾经拉丁语来自希腊语；它描述合乎真实之物。

items.en: Res meant a thing, and realis meant belonging to a thing, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: res 意为事物，realis 意为属于事物的，是整个词族的根。

items.en: English borrowed real to mark what exists rather than what is imagined.
items.cn: 英语借入 real，用来标记存在之物而非想象之物。

items.en: The ending -istic came through Latin from Greek -istikos and forms adjectives of tendency or style.
items.cn: 词尾 -istic 经拉丁语来自希腊语 -istikos，构成表示倾向或风格的形容词。

items.en: The word first described art that copies life, then spread to plans and judgments that accept real limits.
items.cn: 这个词先描述摹写生活的艺术，随后扩展到接受真实限度的计划与判断。

items.en: Modern English uses realistic for practical judgment, lifelike representation, and reachable goals.
items.cn: 现代英语用 realistic 指务实的判断、逼真的表现与可达成的目标。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same root; the near-meaning group gathers words for practical judgment and lifelike quality.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的词；近义组收表示务实判断与逼真品质的词。

entries.definition: To become aware of or make real.
A style that shows life as it is.
Concerned with doing rather than theory.

normalIntro.en: The word applies real in three directions: a mind that faces facts, an image that copies life, and a goal that respects limits.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把 real 用在三个方向：面对事实的心智、摹写生活的影像，以及尊重限度的目标。

normal.en: Realistic is real plus -istic, so it describes whatever keeps close to the real.
normal.cn: realistic 是 real 加 -istic，描述贴近真实之物。

normal.en: A realistic plan accepts what time and money actually allow.
normal.cn: 现实的计划接受时间与金钱的实际限度。

normal.en: A realistic painting copies light and shape so well that the eye is fooled.
normal.cn: 逼真的画把光与形摹得极像，以致骗过眼睛。

normal.en: Be realistic about a job means not expecting more than it can give.
normal.cn: be realistic about a job 意为不对它期望过高。

normal.en: Unrealistic is its direct opposite, built with the negative prefix un-.
normal.cn: unrealistic 是它的直接反义词，由否定前缀 un- 构成。

abstract.en: To be realistic is to measure desire against possibility.
abstract.cn: 现实，就是用可能性来量愿望。

abstract.en: A realistic image is convincing because it obeys the same rules as the eye.
abstract.cn: 逼真的影像之所以可信，因为它遵守与眼睛相同的规则。

abstract.en: Realism is not pessimism; it is the refusal to subtract facts.
abstract.cn: 现实主义不是悲观，而是拒绝把事实减掉。

examples.en: Her plan for the trip was realistic and cheap.
examples.cn: 她的旅行计划现实而省钱。

examples.en: The painting is so realistic that it fools the eye.
examples.cn: 这幅画太逼真了，骗过了眼睛。

examples.en: The team set realistic goals for the first year.
examples.cn: 团队为第一年设定了可行的目标。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞丽斯提克」——画得像真的一样，计划也量力而行，记住 realistic 是现实的、逼真的。

root: 拉丁语 res（事物）→ realis → 英语 real + 后缀 -istic → realistic；同族有 realism、realist、unrealistic。

sensesIntro.en: The core is closeness to the real; the senses divide into practical judgment, lifelike representation, and achievable goals.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「贴近真实」；义项分为务实判断、逼真表现与可达成目标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a still-life painting whose light and shadow almost cannot be told from the objects beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一幅静物画，光影几乎无法与桌边实物分辨。

branches.en: a plan that fits the budget
branches.cn: 贴合预算的计划

branches.en: a painted apple the eye tries to bite
branches.cn: 逼真得让眼睛想去咬的画中苹果

branches.en: a goal set where feet can reach
branches.cn: 设在脚能够到的目标

branches.en: facts accepted and goals kept reachable
branches.cn: 接受事实与保持目标可达

branches.en: an image true to life and a plan true to means
branches.cn: 忠于生活的影像与忠于财力的计划

intro.en: The word is a Latin root with a learned suffix, and its family spreads across art, thought and practice.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁词根加学术词尾，其词族分布在艺术、思想与实践之间。

latinIntro.en: Latin res, a thing, and realis, belonging to a thing, are the recorded sources of the root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 res（事物）与 realis（属于事物的）是这个词根有记录可考的来源。

items.meaning: a style showing life as it is

definition_zh: 现实；实际情况；真实性
definition_en: the state of things as they actually exist; the quality of being real rather than imagined; the facts of a situation
core_image: 清晨菜市场里嘈杂而实实在在的景象
scene: 清晨的菜市场人声嘈杂，泥水沾在菜叶上，一切都实实在在。The reality of the job was harder than the advertisement suggested.
sceneCN: 这里 reality 是「现实」（第 1 个义项：实际存在的情形）；句意为这份工作的现实比广告上说的更难。画面里可留意：嘈杂的市场、沾泥的菜叶、忙碌的人群。

derivatives.zh: real 加 -istic，指现实的、逼真的
un- 与 reality 复合，指不真实、虚幻

senses.title: The world as it exists
senses.definition: the state of things as they actually exist, including what is unpleasant or unexpected
senses.definitionCN: 事物实际存在的情形，包括不愉快或出乎意料之处
senses.example: The reality of the job was harder than the advertisement suggested.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作的现实比广告上说的更难。
senses.why: Reality is real plus -ity, so it names the condition of being a thing that exists, not a wish or a picture.
senses.whyCN: reality 是 real 加 -ity，命名「作为存在之物的状态」，而非愿望或画面。

senses.title: Genuineness
senses.definition: the quality of being genuine, true or actual rather than imagined
senses.definitionCN: 真正、真实或实际而非想象的性质
senses.example: The documentary blurs the line between reality and fiction.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片模糊了真实与虚构的界限。
senses.why: The same noun can point at the quality itself: how much of the real is in a thing.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也可指向性质本身：一物之中含有多少真实。

senses.title: Real life on screen
senses.definition: used as a modifier for programmes that show ordinary people in unscripted situations
senses.definitionCN: 用作定语，指展示普通人在无脚本情境中的节目
senses.example: Reality TV has changed what audiences expect from television.
senses.exampleCN: 真人秀改变了观众对电视的期待。
senses.why: Television borrowed the word for shows that claim to record real life rather than act it out.
senses.whyCN: 电视借用了这个词，指声称记录真实生活而非表演的节目。

intro.en: Reality is real with the Latin noun ending -ity, and its remote source is Latin res, a thing; it names the condition of being real.
intro.cn: reality 是 real 加拉丁名词词尾 -ity，其更早来源是拉丁语 res（事物）；它命名「真实的状况」。

items.en: Res meant a thing or a fact, the plain word for what exists.
items.cn: res 意为事物或事实，是「存在之物」的朴素说法。

items.en: Realitas meant the quality of being real, formed from realis with the noun ending -itas.
items.cn: realitas 意为真实的性质，由 realis 加名词词尾 -itas 构成。

items.en: English took the word as reality, keeping the sense of the way things actually stand.
items.cn: 英语把这个词借作 reality，保留「事物实际如何」的意思。

items.en: The word served for hard facts, then for television that claims to show life unscripted.
items.cn: 这个词先用于硬邦邦的事实，后用于声称展示无脚本生活的电视节目。

items.en: Modern English uses reality for the actual world, for genuineness, and for real-life television.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reality 指实际世界、真实性与真人生活类电视。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same root; the near-meaning group gathers words for fact and actual existence.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的词；近义组收表示事实与实际存在的词。

entries.definition: The state of existing in fact.

normalIntro.en: The word names the condition of being real, then the hard facts of a situation, then television that claims to show life as it is.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词命名「真实的状况」，再指处境的硬事实，最后指声称展示真实生活的电视。

normal.en: Reality is real plus -ity, the noun for being real.
normal.cn: reality 是 real 加 -ity，表示「真实」的名词。

normal.en: In reality is the phrase for saying what actually happens, as opposed to what seems to.
normal.cn: in reality 是用来说实际发生什么、而非看似如何的短语。

normal.en: Face reality means to accept facts you would rather avoid.
normal.cn: face reality 意为接受你宁愿回避的事实。

normal.en: A dream becomes a reality when it stops being only imagined.
normal.cn: 梦想 stop 只是想象时，就成了现实。

normal.en: Reality TV claims to record ordinary life without a script.
normal.cn: reality TV 声称无脚本地记录普通生活。

abstract.en: Reality is what does not disappear when you stop believing in it.
abstract.cn: 现实，是你不再相信时也不会消失的东西。

abstract.en: Every plan meets reality at the point where it must change.
abstract.cn: 每个计划都在必须改变之处遇上现实。

abstract.en: The word reality is often used to end an argument that facts have already won.
abstract.cn: reality 一词常被用来终结一场事实早已获胜的争论。

examples.en: The reality of the job was harder than the advertisement suggested.
examples.cn: 这份工作的现实比广告上说的更难。

examples.en: The documentary blurs the line between reality and fiction.
examples.cn: 这部纪录片模糊了真实与虚构的界限。

examples.en: Reality TV has changed what audiences expect from television.
examples.cn: 真人秀改变了观众对电视的期待。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞阿勒提」——菜市场的泥水与吆喝都实实在在，记住 reality 是现实、真实性。

root: 拉丁语 res（事物）→ realis → realitas → 英语 reality；同族有 real、realistic、realize、unreality。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the condition of being real; the senses divide into the actual world, genuineness, and real-life television.

branches.cn: 黎明时沾泥的菜市场

definition_zh: 领域；王国；界
definition_en: a field or area of activity, knowledge or interest; a kingdom or country ruled by a monarch; a major division of the natural world
core_image: 地图上由边界线围起的一片土地
scene: 地图摊在桌上，边界线把一片土地清清楚楚地围起来。The realm of insects is far larger than most people imagine.
sceneCN: 这里 realm 是「领域」（第 1 个义项：某一活动或知识的范围）；句意为昆虫的领域远比多数人想象的大。画面里可留意：摊开的地图、清楚的边界线、围起的土地。

derivatives.zh: 与 realm 同源的拉丁词，指王室的
与 realm 同源的拉丁词，指政权、制度

senses.title: A field or area
senses.definition: a field or area of activity, knowledge or interest
senses.definitionCN: 活动、知识或兴趣的一个范围
senses.example: The realm of insects is far larger than most people imagine.
senses.exampleCN: 昆虫的领域远比多数人想象的大。
senses.why: A realm was first a territory with borders, and a field of study is also a territory with borders, so the word extended to knowledge.
senses.whyCN: realm 最初指有边界的领土，而一个研究领域也是有边界的领土，于是这个词扩展到知识。

senses.title: A kingdom
senses.definition: a country or kingdom ruled by a monarch
senses.definitionCN: 由君主统治的国家或王国
senses.example: The old realm was divided among three kings.
senses.exampleCN: 这个古老的王国被三位国王瓜分。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a land under a ruler, the territory that a king actually governs.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「君主统治下的土地」，即国王实际治理的疆域。

senses.title: A division of nature
senses.definition: one of the great divisions of the natural world, such as animals, plants or fungi
senses.definitionCN: 自然世界的主要划分之一，如动物界、植物界或真菌界
senses.example: Fungi form a realm of their own, neither plant nor animal.
senses.exampleCN: 真菌自成—界，既非植物也非动物。
senses.why: Science borrowed the word for the largest divisions of living things, because each is a territory with its own borders.
senses.whyCN: 科学借这个词指生物最大的几大划分，因为每一界都是有自身边界的领土。

intro.en: Realm comes from Old French reaume, a kingdom, from Latin regimen, rule, and regere, to rule; English narrowed the spelling but kept the territory.
intro.cn: realm 来自古法语 reaume（王国），源于拉丁语 regimen（统治）与 regere（统治）；英语改变了拼写，却保留了「领土」之意。

items.en: Regere meant to rule or guide straight, and it is the source of regal, regime and region as well.
items.cn: regere 意为统治或引直，也是 regal、regime、region 的来源。

items.en: Regimen meant rule or government, the act by which a territory is held.
items.cn: regimen 意为统治或治理，是维系一片领土的行为。

items.en: Old French reaume named the kingdom itself, the land that a ruler governs.
items.cn: 古法语 reaume 命名王国本身，即统治者所治理的土地。

items.en: Middle English shortened the spelling toward realm but kept the sense of a ruled territory.
items.cn: 中古英语把拼写缩短为 realm，但保留「被统治的领土」之意。

items.en: Modern English uses realm for a kingdom, for any bounded field of activity, and for a division of nature.
items.cn: 现代英语用 realm 指王国、任何有边界的活动领域，以及自然界的一大划分。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same ruling root; the near-meaning group gathers words for territory and field.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「统治」词根的词；近义组收表示领土与范围的词。

entries.definition: Belonging to a king or queen.
A system or government of rule.
A country ruled by a king or queen.
entries.definitionCN: 由国王或女王统治的国家。

entries.definition: An area of activity or knowledge.
A branch of study or activity.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或活动的一个分支。

entries.definition: A area of activity or influence.

normalIntro.en: The word begins as a ruled territory, then becomes any bounded field, and finally a great division of nature.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「被统治的领土」开始，随后成为任何有边界的领域，最后成为自然界的一大划分。

normal.en: Realm, regal, regime and region all come from the Latin word for rule.
normal.cn: realm、regal、regime、region 都来自拉丁语中表示「统治」的词。

normal.en: A realm is a territory with borders, whether a kingdom or a field of study.
normal.cn: realm 是有边界的领土，可以是王国，也可以是研究领域。

normal.en: The realm of nature is a phrase for the whole living world.
normal.cn: the realm of nature 指整个生命世界的说法。

normal.en: Within the realm of is the phrase for saying what an idea belongs to.
normal.cn: within the realm of 是用来说明某观念属于哪个范围的短语。

normal.en: A realm can be expanded, as a kingdom adds land or a science adds subjects.
normal.cn: realm 可以扩展，正如王国增添土地、科学增添科目。

abstract.en: Every realm is made by the border drawn around it.
abstract.cn: 每一个 realm 都由围在它周围的边界造成。

abstract.en: To enter a new realm is to accept its rules.
abstract.cn: 进入一个新的领域，就是接受它的规则。

abstract.en: The realm of the possible is wider than the realm of the permitted.
abstract.cn: 可能的领域比被允许的领域更宽。

examples.en: The realm of insects is far larger than most people imagine.
examples.cn: 昆虫的领域远比多数人想象的大。

examples.en: The old realm was divided among three kings.
examples.cn: 这个古老的王国被三位国王瓜分。

examples.en: Fungi form a realm of their own, neither plant nor animal.
examples.cn: 真菌自成一界，既非植物也非动物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞尔姆」——地图上一圈边界围起的土地，记住 realm 是领域、王国。

root: 拉丁语 regere（统治）→ regimen（统治）→ 古法语 reaume → 中古英语 realm；同族有 regal、regime、region。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a bordered territory; the senses divide into a kingdom, a field of activity, and a division of nature.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「有边界的领土」；义项分为王国、活动领域，以及自然界的一大划分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stretch of land enclosed by a clearly drawn border on a map.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上一片被清楚画出的边界围住的土地。

branches.en: a subject with its own borders
branches.cn: 有自身边界的学科

branches.en: a king's land on an old map
branches.cn: 古地图上国王的土地

branches.en: fungi set apart from plants and animals
branches.cn: 与动植物分开的真菌

branches.en: a field of study and a kingdom, both bordered
branches.cn: 研究领域与王国，都有边界

branches.en: a kingdom of land and a kingdom of living things
branches.cn: 土地的王國与生物的王國

intro.en: The word is a French borrowing from a Latin root, and its family spreads across rule, place and knowledge.

latinIntro.en: Latin regere, to rule, and regimen, rule, are the recorded sources of the family.

definition_zh: 后部；后面的；抚养；饲养；抬起
definition_en: the back part of something; at or toward the back; to bring up a child; to breed animals; to raise something, especially the head
core_image: 马车后轮与车厢尾部
scene: 马车停在院门口，车尾对着台阶，后轮还沾着泥。He turned and walked toward the rear of the house.
sceneCN: 这里 rear 是「后部」（第 1 个义项：某物的后面部分）；句意为马车停在院门口，他转身朝房子后部走去。画面里可留意：马车尾部、后轮上的泥、台阶。

senses.title: The back part
senses.definition: the back part of a building, vehicle or object
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、车辆或物体的后面部分
senses.example: He turned and walked toward the rear of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他转身朝房子后部走去。
senses.why: The back sense came from Old French riere and Latin retro, both meaning behind, and it names the part that lies at the back.
senses.whyCN: 「后面」之义来自古法语 riere 与拉丁语 retro，二者都意为「在后」，它命名位于后方的部分。

senses.title: At the back
senses.definition: located at or toward the back
senses.definitionCN: 位于后方或朝后的
senses.example: The rear window was steamed up with rain.
senses.exampleCN: 后窗被雨水蒙上了水汽。
senses.why: The adjective simply applies the back sense to a noun, marking the part that sits behind the rest.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把「后面」的意思用于名词，标记位于其余部分之后的那一部分。

senses.title: To bring up a child
senses.definition: to care for a child until it is grown
senses.definitionCN: 照料孩子直到其长大
senses.example: She reared three children on her own.
senses.exampleCN: 她独自抚养了三个孩子。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different word, Old English ræran, to raise, and raising a child is lifting it toward adulthood.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个词，即古英语 ræran（抬起），抚养孩子就是把他托向成年。

senses.title: To breed animals
senses.definition: to keep and breed animals or grow plants
senses.definitionCN: 饲养并繁殖动物，或栽培植物
senses.example: The farm rears sheep for wool.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场养羊取毛。
senses.why: Animals are also raised up from young to grown, so the raising sense extends from children to livestock.
senses.whyCN: 动物也是从幼小被养到长成，于是「抬起」之义从孩子扩展到牲畜。

senses.title: To raise the head
senses.definition: to lift something, especially the head, often used of an animal or of something emerging
senses.definitionCN: 抬起某物，尤指头，常用于动物或某物冒现
senses.example: The horse reared its head at the sound.
senses.exampleCN: 马听到声音抬起了头。
senses.why: The oldest sense of ræran is to raise physically, and this literal lifting survives in phrases such as rear its head.
senses.whyCN: ræran 最古老的意思就是实际抬起，这种字面抬起保留在 rear its head 等说法中。

intro.en: Rear is really two words that came to share one spelling: the back sense from Old French riere and Latin retro, and the raising sense from Old English ræran.
intro.cn: rear 其实是两个词共用一个拼写：表示「后面」的义项来自古法语 riere 与拉丁语 retro，表示「抬起」的义项来自古英语 ræran。

items.en: Riere meant behind, and it named the back part of a place or a formation.
items.cn: riere 意为在后，命名一处地方或队列的后部。

items.en: Retro meant backward, and it stands behind the back sense of rear as well as words like retrograde.
items.cn: retro 意为向后，它支撑着 rear 的「后面」义以及与 retrograde 等词的关联。

items.en: Ræran meant to raise or bring up, and it is the source of the farming and family senses.
items.cn: ræran 意为抬起或养育，是饲养与抚养义项的来源。

items.en: The two words came to share the spelling rear, so one form now carries both the back and the raising.
items.cn: 两个词共用 rear 这一拼写，于是一个形式同时承载「后面」与「抬起」。

items.en: Modern English uses rear for the back, for what is behind, for bringing up children and animals, and for lifting the head.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rear 指后部、后面的、抚养孩子与饲养动物，以及抬起头。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and one easily confused word; the near-meaning group gathers words for the back and for raising.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式与一个易混词；近义组收表示后方与抚养的词。

entries.definition: To care for and encourage growth.

normalIntro.en: One spelling carries two histories: the back of a thing, and the act of raising a thing up.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拼写承载两段历史：一物的后部，以及把一物抬起来的行为。

normal.en: Rear and rare look alike, but rare means uncommon while rear means the back or to raise.
normal.cn: rear 与 rare 形近，但 rare 意为罕见，rear 意为后部或抬起。

normal.en: The rear of a car is the part behind the driver.
normal.cn: 车的 rear 是司机后面的部分。

normal.en: To rear children is to bring them up, not to put them at the back.
normal.cn: to rear children 是抚养他们，不是把他们放到后面。

normal.en: To rear cattle is to keep and breed them on a farm.
normal.cn: to rear cattle 是在农场饲养并繁殖牛。

normal.en: A problem rears its head when it suddenly appears.
normal.cn: 问题 rears its head，就是它突然冒出来。

abstract.en: The back and the act of raising share a spelling but not a history.
abstract.cn: 「后部」与「抬起」共用一个拼写，却不共有一段历史。

abstract.en: What is reared is brought from behind to the front of life.
abstract.cn: 被抚养之物，是从后头被带到生命的前台。

abstract.en: To look to the rear is to remember where you came from.
abstract.cn: 看向 rear，就是回望你从何处来。

examples.en: He turned and walked toward the rear of the house.
examples.cn: 他转身朝房子后部走去。

examples.en: The rear window was steamed up with rain.
examples.cn: 后窗被雨水蒙上了水汽。

examples.en: She reared three children on her own.
examples.cn: 她独自抚养了三个孩子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「马车尾部」——后轮沾着泥，记住 rear 是后部、后面的；也指抚养、抬起。

root: 「后部」义：古法语 riere / 拉丁语 retro（在后）；「抬起、抚养」义：古英语 ræran（抬起）。同族有 rearward、rearmost。

sensesIntro.en: One form holds two histories; the senses divide into the back part, the back position, bringing up the young, breeding animals, and lifting the head.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个形式承载两段历史；义项分为后部、后面的位置、抚养幼者、饲养动物，以及抬起头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the back wheels and tail of a carriage standing at a gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：停在院门口的马车后轮与车尾。

branches.en: the tail end of a carriage
branches.cn: 马车的尾部

branches.en: a window at the back of a house
branches.cn: 房子后部的窗

branches.en: a mother raising three children
branches.cn: 抚养三个孩子的母亲

branches.en: sheep bred for wool on a farm
branches.cn: 农场里为取毛而饲养的羊

branches.en: a horse lifting its head at a sound
branches.cn: 听到声音抬起头的马

intro.en: The word joins two origins under one spelling, and its family is built with English suffixes and phrases.
intro.cn: 这个词在同一拼写下汇合两个来源，其词族由英语后缀与短语构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin retro, backward, is the recorded source of the back sense; the raising sense is native Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 retro（向后）是「后面」义有记录可考的来源；「抬起」义则是古英语本族。

items.meaning: to stand on the hind legs

definition_zh: 原因；理由；理性；道理；推理；说服
definition_en: a cause or justification for something; the power of logical thought; good sense or fairness; to think logically; to persuade someone by argument
core_image: 白板上一条从问题连到答案的清晰线
scene: 白板上，一条线从问题连到答案，每一步都标得清楚。There is no reason to doubt her story.
sceneCN: 这里 reason 是「理由」（第 1 个义项：支持某判断的根据）；句意为没有理由怀疑她的说法。画面里可留意：白板上连到答案的线、标清楚的每一步。

derivatives.zh: reason 加 -able，指合理的、公道的
reason 加 -ed，指经过推理的、有条理的

senses.title: A cause or justification
senses.definition: a cause or explanation that justifies something
senses.definitionCN: 为某事提供根据的原因或解释
senses.example: There is no reason to doubt her story.
senses.exampleCN: 没有理由怀疑她的说法。
senses.why: Latin ratio meant a reckoning, and a reason is the reckoning that stands behind a claim or an event.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ratio 意为计算，而理由就是支撑一个说法或事件的那笔「计算」。

senses.title: The power of logical thought
senses.definition: the human power of thinking logically and drawing conclusions
senses.definitionCN: 进行逻辑思考并得出结论的心智能力
senses.example: Reason separates a careful judge from a rash one.
senses.exampleCN: 理性把谨慎的判断者与草率者区分开来。
senses.why: The same reckoning that gives a reason for a claim is also the faculty that performs the reckoning, so reason names the mind's calculating power.
senses.whyCN: 支撑说法的计算，也是完成计算的能力，因此 reason 指心智的计算力。

senses.title: Good sense or fairness
senses.definition: good sense, fairness or what is right in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 良好判断、公平，或处境中正确之事
senses.example: There is reason in what she says, even if we disagree.
senses.exampleCN: 她的话里有道理，即使我们不同意。
senses.why: What follows reason is felt as right and fair, so the word came to name the quality of being in accordance with good sense.
senses.whyCN: 合乎理性之事被感受为正确而公平，于是这个词也命名「合乎常理」的品质。

senses.title: To think logically
senses.definition: to think through facts and form a judgment by logic
senses.definitionCN: 梳理事实并用逻辑形成判断
senses.example: He reasoned that the letter must have been sent yesterday.
senses.exampleCN: 他推断这封信一定是昨天寄出的。
senses.why: Reason as a verb is simply the mind doing what the noun names: reckoning from facts toward a conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 作动词的 reason 就是心智做名词所指之事：从事实推算到结论。

senses.title: To persuade by argument
senses.definition: to persuade someone by presenting arguments rather than force
senses.definitionCN: 通过提出论据而非强力来说服某人
senses.example: She tried to reason with the angry customer.
senses.exampleCN: 她试着与愤怒的顾客讲道理。
senses.why: When reasoning is aimed at another person, the verb means to bring that person's mind into line through argument.
senses.whyCN: 当推理指向另一个人时，这个动词便指通过论证把对方的心拉到同一线上。

intro.en: Reason comes from Old French reisun, from Latin ratio, reckoning and reason, which itself comes from reri, to reckon or think.
intro.cn: reason 来自古法语 reisun，源于拉丁语 ratio（计算与理性），而 ratio 又来自 reri（计算、思考）。

items.en: Reri meant to reckon or think, the act behind every form of this family.
items.cn: reri 意为计算或思考，是整个词族背后的动作。

items.en: Ratio meant a reckoning and also the faculty of reason that makes reckoning possible.
items.cn: ratio 意为计算，也指使计算成为可能的理性能力。

items.en: Old French reisun carried the word to English with the sense of a cause and of good judgment.
items.cn: 古法语 reisun 把这个词带到英语，带着「原因」与「良好判断」的意思。

items.en: Middle English reason kept both the explanation and the thinking power, and added the verb.
items.cn: 中古英语 reason 既保留解释，也保留思维能力，并加上了动词用法。

items.en: Modern English uses reason for causes, for the thinking power, for fairness, for logical argument, and for persuading.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reason 指原因、思维能力、公平、逻辑论证，以及说服。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same reckoning root; the near-meaning group gathers words for cause, logic and persuasion.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「计算」词根的词；近义组收表示原因、逻辑与说服的词。

entries.definition: A reason for acting in a certain way.
entries.definitionCN: 以某种方式行动的理由。

normalIntro.en: The word is reckoning: it names the cause behind an event, the mind that reckons, the fairness that reckoning yields, and the acts of reasoning and persuading.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是「计算」：它命名事件背后的原因、进行计算的心智、计算带来的公平，以及推理与说服的行为。

normal.en: Reason and ratio come from the same Latin word for reckoning.
normal.cn: reason 与 ratio 来自同一个表示「计算」的拉丁词。

normal.en: The reason for a thing is the explanation that stands behind it.
normal.cn: 一物的 reason，就是站在它背后的解释。

normal.en: Reason as a power is what lets a person follow an argument.
normal.cn: 作为能力的 reason，使人能够跟上论证。

normal.en: Within reason means inside the limits of what makes sense.
normal.cn: within reason 意为在合乎情理的限度之内。

normal.en: To reason with someone is to argue calmly rather than force them.
normal.cn: to reason with 某人，是平静论理而非强迫对方。

abstract.en: A reason is a bridge between a fact and a conclusion.
abstract.cn: reason 是事实与结论之间的一座桥。

abstract.en: Reason can be used to justify almost anything, which is why it needs honesty.
abstract.cn: 理性几乎可以为任何事辩护，因此它需要诚实。

abstract.en: To lose one's reason is to lose the bridge, not the world.
abstract.cn: 失去理智，是失去那座桥，而不是失去世界。

examples.en: There is no reason to doubt her story.
examples.cn: 没有理由怀疑她的说法。

examples.en: He reasoned that the letter must have been sent yesterday.
examples.cn: 他推断这封信一定是昨天寄出的。

examples.en: She tried to reason with the angry customer.
examples.cn: 她试着与愤怒的顾客讲道理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「白板上连到答案的线」——每一步都有根据，记住 reason 是原因、理由、理性。

root: 拉丁语 reri（计算、思考）→ ratio（计算、理性）→ 古法语 reisun → 英语 reason；同族有 reasonable、reasoning、ratio。

sensesIntro.en: The core is reckoning; the senses divide into a cause, the thinking power, fairness, logical argument, and persuasion.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「计算」；义项分为原因、思维能力、公平、逻辑论证与说服。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line on a whiteboard running from a question to its answer, every step marked.
core.cn: 核心意象：白板上一条从问题连到答案的线，每一步都标得清楚。

branches.en: a cause written under an event
branches.cn: 写在事件下方的成因

branches.en: a careful mind following a proof
branches.cn: 跟着证明走的谨慎心智

branches.en: a fair answer that satisfies both sides
branches.cn: 让双方都服气的公道答复

branches.en: steps joined from fact to conclusion
branches.cn: 从事实连到结论的步骤

branches.en: two people arguing until one agrees
branches.cn: 争论到一方同意的两个人

intro.en: The word is a French borrowing from a Latin root, and its family is built with English suffixes and phrases.
intro.cn: 这个词是源自拉丁词根的法语借词，其词族由英语后缀与短语构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin reri, to reckon, and ratio, reckoning, are the recorded sources of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 reri（计算）与 ratio（计算）是这个词族有记录可考的来源。

items.meaning: a cause or the thinking power

definition_zh: 合理的；公道的；还算好的
definition_en: sensible and fair, based on good reason; fair in price; moderate in amount and acceptable
core_image: 天平两端重量相当，指针停在正中
scene: 天平两端的重量差不多，指针稳稳停在正中。The hotel charges a reasonable price for the room.
sceneCN: 这里 reasonable 是「公道的」（第 2 个义项：价格公平、不离谱）；句意为这家酒店的房间价格公道。画面里可留意：平衡的天平、停在正中的指针、价目牌。

pos.zh: 合理的；公道的；还算好的

derivatives.zh: reasonable 的词根，指理由、理性
reasonable 加 -ly，指合理地、相当地
un- 与 reasonable 复合，指不合理的

senses.title: Sensible and fair
senses.definition: based on good reason and fair to those involved
senses.definitionCN: 基于充分理由，且对相关各方公平
senses.example: She gave a reasonable explanation for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 她为延误给出了合理的解释。
senses.why: Reasonable is reason plus -able, so it describes what can be supported by reason and accepted as fair.
senses.whyCN: reasonable 是 reason 加 -able，描述能被理由支持、并被接受为公平的事物。

senses.title: Fair in price
senses.definition: of a price, not too high and fair for what is offered
senses.definitionCN: 指价格不过高，与所提供之物相称
senses.example: The hotel charges a reasonable price for the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店的房间价格公道。
senses.why: A price that reason can approve is one that is not excessive, so the word came to mean fair in price.
senses.whyCN: 理性能够认可的价格，就是不过分的价格，于是这个词引申为「价格公道」。

senses.title: Moderate and acceptable
senses.definition: of an amount, moderate but enough to be acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 指数量适中但足以令人接受
senses.example: There was a reasonable amount of time to finish the work.
senses.exampleCN: 完成这项工作有相当充裕的时间。
senses.why: What stays within reason is neither tiny nor excessive, so the word marks a moderate amount that still satisfies.
senses.whyCN: 合乎理性之物既不过小也不过量，因此这个词标记一个适中却仍令人满意的数量。

intro.en: Reasonable is reason plus the ending -able, meaning able to be supported by reason; reason itself goes back to Latin ratio.
intro.cn: reasonable 是 reason 加词尾 -able，意为能被理由支持的；reason 本身可追溯到拉丁语 ratio。

items.en: Ratio meant reckoning and reason, the standard against which a claim is judged.
items.cn: ratio 意为计算与理性，是评判一个说法的标准。

items.en: English reason carries both the cause behind a thing and the mind's power of judging.
items.cn: 英语 reason 既承载事物背后的原因，也承载心智的判断力。

items.en: The ending -able means able to be, so reason plus -able is able to be justified by reason.
items.cn: 词尾 -able 意为「能被……的」，因此 reason 加 -able 就是「能被理性证明的」。

items.en: A sum that reason approves is fair, and an amount that reason accepts is moderate.
items.cn: 理性认可的数额是公道的，理性接受的数量是适中的。

items.en: Modern English uses reasonable for fair judgment, fair prices, and moderate but acceptable amounts.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reasonable 指公平的判断、公道的价格，以及适中却可接受的数量。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the reason root; the near-meaning group gathers words for fairness and moderation.
note.cn: 形近组收 reason 词根的词；近义组收表示公平与适中的词。

entries.definition: A cause or the thinking power.
Neither too much nor too little.

normalIntro.en: The word asks whether reason can approve: a fair judgment, a fair price, and a moderate amount all pass that test.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词问的是理性能否认可：公平的判断、公道的价格、适中的数量都能通过这一检验。

normal.en: Reasonable is reason plus -able, so it means able to be justified by reason.
normal.cn: reasonable 是 reason 加 -able，意为能被理性证明的。

normal.en: A reasonable price is one that does not ask too much.
normal.cn: 公道的价格，是不过分索价的价格。

normal.en: A reasonable explanation is one that holds together and is fair.
normal.cn: 合理的解释，是前后一致且公平的解释。

normal.en: Be reasonable about a delay means do not react with anger.
normal.cn: be reasonable about a delay 意为不要动怒。

normal.en: Unreasonable is the opposite, built with the negative prefix un-.
normal.cn: unreasonable 是反义词，由否定前缀 un- 构成。

abstract.en: Reasonable is the meeting point of logic and fairness.
abstract.cn: reasonable 是逻辑与公平的交汇处。

abstract.en: What is reasonable to one person may still be too much for another.
abstract.cn: 对一个人合理的，对另一个人也许仍然过分。

abstract.en: To be reasonable is to leave room for the other side.
abstract.cn: 讲道理，就是给对方留下余地。

examples.en: She gave a reasonable explanation for the delay.
examples.cn: 她为延误给出了合理的解释。

examples.en: The hotel charges a reasonable price for the room.
examples.cn: 这家酒店的房间价格公道。

examples.en: There was a reasonable amount of time to finish the work.
examples.cn: 完成这项工作有相当充裕的时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「天平停在正中」——两边重量相当，价格与道理都不过分，记住 reasonable 是合理的、公道的。

root: 拉丁语 reri（计算）→ ratio（理性）→ 古法语 reisun → 英语 reason + 后缀 -able → reasonable；同族有 reasonably、unreasonable。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「理性能够认可」；义项分为公平判断、公道价格，以及适中可接受的数量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance whose two pans hold equal weight, the needle steady at the centre.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平两端重量相当，指针稳稳停在正中。

branches.en: an explanation that holds together
branches.cn: 前后一致的解释

branches.en: a price card that does not shock
branches.cn: 不会让人吃惊的价目牌

branches.en: enough time to finish without strain
branches.cn: 从容完成的时间

branches.en: a fair judgment and a fair price
branches.cn: 公平的判断与公道的价格

branches.en: a moderate price and a moderate amount
branches.cn: 适中的价格与适中的数量

intro.cn: 这个词是 reason 加英语后缀，其背后有拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin ratio, reckoning and reason, is the recorded source of the root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ratio（计算与理性）是这个词根有记录可考的来源。

items.meaning: a cause or the thinking power

definition_zh: 反叛者；武装反抗；抗拒常规
definition_en: a person who rises against authority; to rise against authority; to refuse accepted rules
core_image: 举着火把的人群背对王座站成一排
scene: 广场上人群举着火把，把印着徽章的旗帜倒转过来。The rebel forces refused to surrender.
sceneCN: 这里 rebel 作定语，指「反叛者」（第 1 个义项：拿起武器反叛的人）；句意为叛军拒绝投降。画面里可留意：倒转的旗帜、背对王座的人群。

senses.title: A person who rises against authority
senses.definition: a person who takes up arms or openly refuses to obey those in power
senses.definitionCN: 拿起武器或公开拒绝服从当权者的人
senses.example: The rebel was arrested at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 那名反叛者在黎明时被捕。
senses.why: The Latin rebellis meant one who renews war, and the noun kept that image of a person who reopens a fight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rebellis 意为重新开战的人，名词保留了「重新掀起战斗」这一意象。

senses.title: To rise against authority
senses.definition: to fight against a government or a ruling power
senses.definitionCN: 与政府或统治力量作战
senses.example: The peasants rebelled against the heavy taxes.
senses.exampleCN: 农民们反抗沉重的赋税。
senses.why: The verb was formed from the noun, turning the person who renews war into the act of renewing it.
senses.whyCN: 动词由名词而来，把「重新开战的人」转成了「重新开战」这一行为。

senses.title: To resist accepted rules
senses.definition: to refuse to accept the habits or rules of a group, often in a personal way
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝接受某个群体的习惯或规则，常带个人色彩
senses.example: Teenagers often rebel against their parents' advice.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年常常抗拒父母的建议。
senses.why: Rebellion moved from the battlefield into daily life, where refusing advice is a small war of one's own.
senses.whyCN: 反叛从战场走进日常生活，拒绝建议就是一个人自己的小战争。

intro.en: Rebel carries war inside it: a Latin word for war sits at its centre, joined to a prefix meaning again.
intro.cn: rebel 内部藏着战争：拉丁语的「战争」一词就在它中间，并与表「再次」的前缀相连。

items.en: Bellum meant war, the raw material of every rebellion.
items.cn: bellum 意为战争，是一切反叛的原材料。

items.en: The prefix re- added the idea of again or in return, giving renewed war.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 加上「再次」或「回击」的意思，构成「重新开战」。

items.en: Rebellis described both a renewed war and the person who waged it.
items.cn: rebellis 既指重新开战的战争，也指发动它的人。

items.en: Old French rebelle carried the person and the act into English.
items.cn: 古法语 rebelle 把人与其行为一起带入英语。

items.en: Modern English uses rebel for the person, for the act, and for a personal refusal of rules.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rebel 指人、指行为，也指个人对规则的抗拒。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs and nouns close in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for armed and unarmed resistance.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近的动词与名词；近义组收表武装与非武装抵抗的词。

entries.definition: To drive back or push away.
One who rises in armed revolt.

normalIntro.en: The word keeps the Latin word for war at its centre, so every sense carries a small battlefield.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词中间藏着拉丁语的「战争」，因此每个义项都带着一小片战场。

normal.en: Re plus bellum: making war again is the oldest picture of a rebel.
normal.cn: re 加 bellum：重新开战，就是 rebel 最古老的画面。

normal.en: A rebel can be a person or an act, so one spelling serves noun and verb.
normal.cn: rebel 既可指人也可指行为，同一拼写兼作名词与动词。

normal.en: The noun stress falls on the first syllable, the verb stress on the second.
normal.cn: 名词重音在第一音节，动词重音在第二音节。

normal.en: Rebel against is the phrase for refusing a person or a rule.
normal.cn: rebel against 是拒绝某人或某条规则的固定搭配。

normal.en: Rebellion and rebellious grow from the same root, one an act and one a trait.
normal.cn: rebellion 与 rebellious 同根，一个指行为，一个指性格。

abstract.en: Every rebel begins by deciding that an old order no longer deserves obedience.
abstract.cn: 每个反叛者都从判定旧秩序不再值得服从开始。

abstract.en: Rebellion is renewal with a cost, a war fought again in a smaller room.
abstract.cn: 反叛是带代价的更新，是在更小的房间里再打一场战争。

abstract.en: To rebel against advice is to claim the right to make one's own mistakes.
abstract.cn: 抗拒建议，就是主张自己犯错的权利。

examples.cn: 那名反叛者在黎明时被捕。

examples.en: The peasants rebelled against the heavy taxes.
examples.cn: 农民们反抗沉重的赋税。

examples.en: Teenagers often rebel against their parents' advice.
examples.cn: 青少年常常抗拒父母的建议。

root: 拉丁 bellum（战争）→ 前缀 re-（再次）→ 拉丁 rebellis（重新开战者）→ 古法语 rebelle → 英语 rebel；同族有 rebellion、rebellious。

sensesIntro.en: The core is renewed war; the senses cover the person, the act, and the everyday refusal of rules.

core.cn: 核心意象：人群举着火把，背对王座站成一排。

branches.en: a figure with a raised torch
branches.cn: 高举火把的身影

branches.en: a village rising in arms
branches.cn: 拿起武器的村庄

branches.en: a teenager turning away from advice
branches.cn: 扭头不听建议的少年

branches.en: the person and the uprising
branches.cn: 人与起义
